title: A little room to change our minds
audience: Developers trying the guide's camera moves, grounded answers, live interruptions, editable itinerary, and surface-site viewing through a short, friendly astronomy visit.
introduction: Let's take a short trip with room to change our minds. You'll see our stops laid out, and you can interrupt me whenever something catches your interest. We'll start at Saturn and finish near the Moon.

stops.subject: Saturn
stops.objective: Explore Saturn's rings from a new angle, and choose your own view.
stops.narration: Galileo once saw odd little ears beside Saturn. His telescope couldn't show him the rings clearly. Let's ease around and open up their shape. You can ask for a different angle while we talk; there's plenty here worth lingering over.
cameraIdeas: Request the available Saturn reveal composition and wait for arrival before starting this stop's narration.
During the narration, gently open the viewing angle on the rings, retaining the whole main ring system in frame and staying outside it.
After the final sentence, allow minimumViewSeconds of quiet viewing before the next stop.

stops.subject: Titan
stops.objective: Get to know Titan's strange weather, with room for your questions.
stops.narration: Titan has methane rain and rivers, with water ice taking the role of rock. Strange weather, familiar shapes. As we drift closer, ask for the astronomy behind it, or for this moon's measurements recorded in the planetarium we're exploring together.
cameraIdeas: Request an available Titan composition and wait for arrival before starting this stop's narration.
Use a gentle push-in during the narration, keeping Titan's whole globe and atmosphere comfortably in frame.
After the final sentence, allow minimumViewSeconds of quiet viewing; do not imply individual rivers are visible.

stops.subject: Moon
stops.objective: Pause by the Moon, consider Apollo's footprints, and choose where we go next.
stops.narration: Let's settle here for a moment. Apollo's trails linger because the Moon has no wind or rain to erase them. A closer view makes a good place for questions. You can interrupt me and change where we go next.
cameraIdeas: If the current inventory returns a Moon surface site, request a view using that returned site ID. Otherwise, request an available exterior Moon composition; do not invent a site.
Wait for the requested site's arrival, or the fallback composition's arrival, before starting this stop's narration, then hold the camera still.
The Apollo story is historical context; do not imply the selected site is an Apollo site or that tracks are rendered.
After the narration, hold silently for minimumViewSeconds, then speak the closing without moving away.

sources.title: NASA Science: 10 cool things NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter is teaching us about the Moon

closing: Try 'add Jupiter,' ask a question, or tell me to skip or reorder a stop. The plan you see will follow along. You can also say 'pause,' 'next,' 'back,' or 'resume.' We'll keep exploring at your pace.
